verdict: Texas Instruments' revenue rose 19% to $4.83B as Analog sales surged 22%, and flat running costs turned that growth into a 31% jump in net income to $1.55B.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: in Q1, incl. $555M of CHIPS Act incentive proceeds

segments.name: Analog
segments.note: Analog chips — sensing and power products used in nearly every electronic device; growth led by industrial and data center.

segments.name: Embedded Processing
segments.note: Processors that sit inside cars, appliances and factory equipment.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: DLP products, calculators and custom chips.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: R&D — designing new analog and embedded chips; down slightly from $517M a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and the back office (SG&A); down slightly from $472M a year ago.

opex.name: Acquisition charges
opex.note: Charges tied to acquisitions; none a year ago.

otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was $47M, less $141M of interest and debt expense — a net $94M expense outside operations.
oneTimers: Earnings per share included a 5-cent benefit that was not in the company's original guidance, as stated in the release.
Free cash flow of $1,399M includes $555M of CHIPS Act incentive proceeds received in the quarter.
footerNote: Segment operating profit: Analog $1,638M, Embedded Processing $122M, Other $48M.

takeaways.title: Analog is driving the quarter
takeaways.text: Analog revenue rose 22% to $3.92B with growth led by industrial and data center demand — TI's biggest business did the heavy lifting.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded
takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 58.0% (from 56.9% a year ago) as revenue grew 19% while R&D and SG&A slightly fell — operating profit jumped 37%.

takeaways.title: Cash returned to owners
takeaways.text: TI returned $1,449M in the quarter — $1,291M of dividends and $158M of buybacks; trailing-12-month free cash flow was $4.4B.
